messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean (i.e., the standard error) is calculated as:

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.2215
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
We need to calculate the standard error of the mean? The question: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6." They likely want the standard error: sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). That equals 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean under null: sqrt((sample_std_dev^2)/sample_size). That's same. So answer ~0.2215.

But the tool is for p-value calculation. We could call the function to compute p-value. But the user only asks for standard deviation. We can compute manually. Provide result.
